context: Virulence + AMR gene screen of 3 fish-associated E. faecalis (BFFF11, BFF1B1, BFPS6). Replication verdict: PARTIAL (strong).

open_questions.q: Do the observed virulence-factor and AMR-gene distributions co-occur non-randomly across the three strains, and does the concentration of the entire cps capsule cluster + prgB/asa1 aggregation substances in BFFF11 correlate with a distinct AMR profile relative to BFPS6 (which alone carries the four tet genes)?
open_questions.basis: Paper Table 2 shows that BFFF11 uniquely carries 11 cps genes plus prgB/asa1, while BFPS6 uniquely carries tet(M)/tet(L)/tet(S)/tet(45). Whether this VF/AMR partitioning is a chance draw of 3 genomes or a real ecological/lineage signal is not tested in the paper (n=3 is too small for any statistical claim, and no phylogenetic or PCA-of-gene-presence analysis is presented).
next_steps: Pull 200-500 public E. faecalis genomes from NCBI Pathogen Detection / BV-BRC filtered to fish/aquaculture hosts.
Rerun the same VFDB set-A tblastn + AMRFinderPlus pipeline on all of them to build a presence/absence matrix.
Test for co-occurrence enrichment (Fisher's exact / mutual information) between the cps-cluster+prgB block and specific AMR classes.
Overlay onto an MLST or core-genome phylogeny to see whether the pattern is lineage-linked rather than ecology-linked.

open_questions.q: Are the acquired AMR genes in BFPS6 (tet(M), tet(L), tet(S), tet(45), lsa(A)) chromosomally integrated or carried on mobile genetic elements (plasmids, ICEs, transposons such as Tn916/Tn917), and what is the horizontal-transfer risk to co-cultured fish or human-adjacent Enterococci?
open_questions.basis: The paper does not report any plasmid/ICE/MGE analysis. tet(M) in Enterococci is famously Tn916-family-borne; tet(L) is frequently pT181-family plasmid-borne; lsa(A) is chromosomal in E. faecalis. Without a mobile-element analysis (MobileElementFinder, PlasmidFinder, oriTfinder, ICEfinder) the reader cannot assess whether these are stable chromosomal calls or a horizontal-transfer hazard --- which matters for aquaculture antibiotic-use policy.
next_steps: Run MobileElementFinder + PlasmidFinder + oriTfinder on the three assemblies (BFPS6 is 45 contigs so contig-boundary analysis is required).
Attempt long-read (ONT / PacBio) resequencing of BFPS6 to close the assembly and unambiguously assign each tet gene to a replicon.
Search flanking regions of each tet call for Tn916, Tn917, or IS-element signatures via ISfinder BLAST.
If mobile, do a conjugation experiment (BFPS6 x plasmid-free recipient) to demonstrate transfer competence.

open_questions.q: How sensitive are the reported 69 virulence + 39 AMR gene counts to database version drift and to the specific database mix (VirulenceFinder + VFDB + PATRIC/Victors vs. AMRFinderPlus + ResFinder + CARD + ARG-ANNOT), and would a 2026-era re-run of the same pipeline produce the same totals?
open_questions.basis: The paper aggregates hits across 4 VF and 4 AMR databases without pinning versions or publishing per-database attribution. Our independent AMRFinderPlus DB 2024-07-22.1 run captured lsa(A), tet(L), tet(M) but not tet(S)/tet(45)/mph(D)/dfr(E) --- consistent with the paper's ARG-ANNOT-vs-AMRFinderPlus scope difference, but leaving the 39-gene total unverified. VF total (69) has a similar dependency: ~16 Victors/PATRIC-called VFs were not recoverable from VFDB set-A.
next_steps: Reproduce the paper's exact 8-database matrix at the 2022 versions used by the paper (requires archival container images or version-pinned installs).
Compare against the same 8 databases at their current 2026 versions; report per-database delta.
Publish a per-strain, per-database, per-gene hit table as CSV (not just totals) so downstream re-users can rebuild any count.
Quantify how much of the 69/39 total is unique acquired-resistance vs. mutation-in-target vs. housekeeping-tagged-as-VF.

open_questions.q: What is the minimum assembly-quality threshold (contig count, N50, per-base coverage, contamination rate) required for reliable virulence/AMR gene calling in E. faecalis, and does the 45-contig BFPS6 assembly meet it for the tet-cluster call?
open_questions.basis: BFFF11 and BFF1B1 are closed single-chromosome assemblies (N50 = full chromosome). BFPS6 is 45 contigs, N50 = 270 kb, L50 = 2. Genes spanning contig boundaries (or on short contigs with adjacent MGE remnants) can be miscalled or truncated. The paper does not report per-strain gene-completeness QC or contig-boundary flags for the tet cluster calls that drive its BFPS6-specific claim.
next_steps: For each of the four tet gene calls in BFPS6, report the host contig, contig length, distance-to-contig-edge, and per-base coverage.
Rerun CheckM2 / BUSCO on all three assemblies to quantify completeness/contamination.
Benchmark call sensitivity as a function of simulated contig-fragmentation (shred each closed genome to N50 = 50k, 100k, 250k and see which calls survive).
Recommend a minimum standard (e.g. N50 >= 100 kb, completeness >= 99%, contamination <= 1%, no target gene within 500 bp of a contig edge) for future fish-Enterococcus VF/AMR studies.

open_questions.q: How well do the in-silico VF and AMR gene calls predict phenotype --- specifically, do the four tet-gene BFPS6 calls translate to measurable tetracycline resistance (MIC above CLSI/EUCAST breakpoint), and do the shared VF calls translate to measurable virulence in a fish-infection or Galleria model?
open_questions.basis: The paper is entirely in-silico. No MIC/disk-diffusion data are reported; no infection-model virulence assay is reported. Genotype-to-phenotype gap is a well-known failure mode for AMR prediction (silent genes, disrupted promoters, mutation-inactivated ORFs, regulator loss) and for VF prediction (mere gene presence != expression != pathogenicity).
next_steps: Perform CLSI-standard broth-microdilution MICs for tetracycline, doxycycline, minocycline, erythromycin, clindamycin, and linezolid on all three strains.
For BFPS6 tet-cluster expression: RT-qPCR of tet(M)/tet(L)/tet(S)/tet(45) under induction (sub-inhibitory tetracycline).
Galleria mellonella or zebrafish larva challenge with all three strains at matched CFU doses; report LD50.
Correlate genotype presence-count with phenotype (MIC, LD50) --- test whether BFFF11's cps+prgB block gives higher LD50 than the other two.
